sections.h2: What is Hialeah's story, and how does it affect a sale here?
sections.html:
Hialeah was incorporated in 1925, and the city marked its centennial in 2025. The centennial site traces the name to Muskogee words usually rendered as pretty prairie, and credits aviator Glenn Curtiss and Missouri cattleman James H. Bright with developing the area from 1921. Bright's company with Curtiss also built Miami Springs and Opa-locka.

Hialeah Park opened the same year as the city. It is on the National Register of Historic Places and is also an Audubon Bird Sanctuary. The park is a landmark inside the city, and the centennial site says visitors over the years included figures such as Harry Truman and Winston Churchill. In 1937 it was where Amelia Earhart said goodbye to the United States before her world flight attempt.

sections.h2: Which county bills Hialeah property taxes, and when are bills mailed?
sections.html:
Hialeah is in Miami-Dade County, and the Miami-Dade County Tax Collector sends the bill. The collector's page says the 2026 annual notices were mailed on October 30, 2026, and online payment opened the same day. The office is at 200 NW 2nd Avenue, Miami, and the phone number is 305-375-5448.

The collector does not set the tax. Value comes from the Property Appraiser, less exemptions, and the rate from each taxing authority. If the 2026 real estate taxes are not paid before June 1, 2027, a tax certificate may be issued, and the annual certificate sale starts June 1, 2027.

  • Water, road and sewer assessments, such as OJUS, are collected in annual installments, and a bill containing one must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold for the remaining lien balance.
  • Discounts for paying early step down each month, with the largest in November.

sections.h2: What did Amendment 3 change for a Hialeah homestead?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser's homestead page says voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and that it takes effect January 1, 2027. The change applies to non-school property taxes, and the school board exemption stays at $25,000.

Homestead exemption amounts as printed by the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser
Tax yearUp to, non-school taxes
Through 2026$50,000 (state homestead exemption)
2027$150,000 for residents established by December 31, 2026
2028$250,000 for the same group
2029 onwardAdjusted yearly for positive CPI change

Residents who establish Florida residency after December 31, 2026 start at up to $50,000, and the page says they generally reach the larger amount in the fifth year of receiving a homestead exemption. The page notes that this provision depends on federal constitutional limits and implementing legislation, so a buyer coming from another state should ask the appraiser how the rules apply.

sections.h2: How do you file for, keep or lose homestead in Hialeah?
sections.html:
• Deadline: applications and documents are due March 1, and late applications may be accepted until the date on the TRIM notice, with a possible $15 fee and a Value Adjustment Board petition.
  • Residency proof: one item such as a Florida driver license, vehicle registration, voter registration, a W-2 or tax return, bank statements, utility payments or a recorded Declaration of Domicile.
  • Where: the online Application Portal, or in person at the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1 Street, Suite 710, or the South Dade Government Center. Phone 305-375-4712.
  • Renewal: homestead owners get a renewal receipt in late December, and no receipt goes to properties with a deed change.

Renting the house puts the exemption at risk. If the owner fails to report a change in status, the page says back taxes can reach ten years of exempted taxes, plus 15 percent interest per year and a penalty of 50 percent of the taxes exempted. Report any change before you list the house for rent or sale.

sections.h2: How does Miami-Dade's deed tax differ for a Hialeah seller?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade is the one county with its own rate. The Revenue Department lists 60 cents per $100 on a deed there, plus a 45 cent surtax per $100 that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. All other counties use 70 cents.

The clerk collects the tax at recording. All parties to the deed are liable, whoever the contract says will pay. The Department's list of taxable deeds names quit claim deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure, while a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable. Use the Miami-Dade Clerk's current schedule to confirm the recording charges on your closing statement.

sections.h2: What should a Hialeah owner do about permits and inspections?
sections.html:
Ask the City of Hialeah building department for the permit history of your address, and pull any open or expired permit before you list. Items buyers often ask about are roofs, window replacements, electrical panels, additions and fences.

If the house has unpermitted work, a buyer may require the work to be permitted, repaired or priced in. A cash buyer may accept the house with open items, but a lender-financed buyer usually will not. Get the facts first, then choose the route.

sections.h2: What if you disagree with a Hialeah assessment or an exemption denial?
sections.html:
The state Revenue Department says a value challenge is a petition filed with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and a denial of an exemption can be taken to the value adjustment board 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. The Miami-Dade appraiser mails the proposed notice by the end of August, and the page says the late-filing date shown on it is usually 25 days after mailing.

A sale is a good moment to check the parcel record. Confirm the owner name, the exemptions listed, and the mailing address on the tax roll with the Property Appraiser, so the notice reaches you.

sections.h2: Which ways of selling a Hialeah house are worth comparing?
sections.html:
• Listing with an agent: wider exposure, more showings and inspection requests, and a closing that depends on the buyer's financing.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: a purchase in present condition, with timing you can agree on, and a price you should compare against a listing estimate.
  • Selling to a relative: still a taxable deed event, and it changes the property's assessment if the cap resets.

Whichever you choose, ask each buyer for written terms, the date money reaches you, and who pays recording and deed tax. Keep the Miami-Dade tax bill, any assessment notice and permit records with the contract.

sections.h2: What other Miami-Dade appraiser rules should a Hialeah seller know?
sections.html:
The appraiser's page says an owner who applies for homestead in another Florida county must cancel the Miami-Dade exemption, and that tracking an application is done through a status page. Suspected homestead fraud goes to an investigation unit at 305-375-3402.

The collector's page adds that BillExpress subscribers receive the annual notice by email on the mailing date. A deed change means no renewal receipt, so file a new application after buying.

faqs.a: Miami-Dade County, which means the Miami-Dade Tax Collector and Property Appraiser handle your tax bill and exemptions.
1925. The city celebrated its centennial in 2025.

faqs.q: What is the Miami-Dade deed tax rate?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue lists 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax per $100, and the surtax does not apply to a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: When is the homestead deadline in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: March 1. A late application may still be taken until the date shown on the TRIM notice, and a $15 fee may apply.

faqs.q: What happens if I rent out a homestead house?
faqs.a: The exemption can be lost, and unreported changes can be back taxed for ten years with 15 percent interest and a 50 percent penalty, as the Property Appraiser's page states.
